arguments.title: Resumable at-least-once event consumer with per-event checkpoints
arguments.summary: Builds one file, src/adapter.mjs, that turns a raw at-least-once event stream (one that deliberately repeats the boundary event of every batch) into a clean run() the application can call: it resumes from a server-stored checkpoint, skips events it has already handled, and only advances the checkpoint after each event's handler has actually succeeded -- so a crash mid-batch loses nothing and a later run picks up exactly where the failure happened, not from the start of the batch. Records in integration/manifest.json which of the 10 frozen conformance cases it satisfies, several of which check the exact order of calls, not just the final result. One card: the resume, skip and checkpoint-ordering logic all live in one small run() loop over one shared cursor, so splitting it would only fragment one cohesive algorithm.
arguments.spec:
# Event consumer — integration brief (at-least-once stream, server-side checkpoints)

`service/event-stream-service.mjs` is a DETERMINISTIC, in-process event stream with server-side checkpoints. Its
`request()` ALWAYS returns `{status, body}`, NEVER throws. Write `src/adapter.mjs` so an application can consume
it EXACTLY once per event, resumably.

Routes: `GET /events` (query.limit 1..4, optional query.after) -> `200 {events, nextAfter|null}`; `GET
/checkpoints/:consumer` -> `200 {consumer, after}` or `404 not_found` (no checkpoint stored yet); `PUT
/checkpoints/:consumer {after}` -> `200` or `422 validation_failed`.

AT-LEAST-ONCE delivery: a read with `after: "4"` returns the event whose seq is 4 AND the ones following it -- the
cursor is INCLUSIVE on purpose (the stream would rather repeat an event than lose it). Recognising the repeat is
the consumer's job, not a bug to route around.

`src/adapter.mjs` must export `createEventConsumer(service, options)` -> `{run()}`. `options` carries
`consumerId`, `handle(event)` (may be async, may throw) and `batchSize` (default 4).

The behaviour, EXACTLY:
- Resume: load the stored checkpoint first. A 404 means "never run" -- start from the beginning, and do NOT
  invent a cursor on that first read.
- Read in batches of batchSize, following nextAfter until it is null, then stop.
- Handle EVERY event once, in ascending seq order; an event at or below what has already been handled is a
  re-delivery and must be skipped, not handled again.
- Checkpoint after the work, NEVER before -- the stored `after` must NEVER name an event that has not been handled
  successfully. This is the whole difference between at-least-once and at-most-once: checkpointing first loses
  EVERY event in the window when the process dies mid-batch.
- A throwing handler stops the run and the error propagates; the checkpoint must not cover the failed event, so a
  later run reprocesses from it.
- A non-2xx from the service rejects with an error named ServiceError carrying status and code.

Frozen evidence (do not touch): service/, conformance/, test/integration.test.js, scripts/run-tests.mjs -- digest
checked every run. Deliverable: src/adapter.mjs (replacing the throwing stub) plus integration/manifest.json,
whose `implemented` lists the conformance case ids (C01-C10) that actually pass; several cases read the call log
(the cursor on the first read, the batch limit, and the exact position of the first checkpoint write relative to
the first handled event).
arguments.plan:
One card. Implement src/adapter.mjs: run() first GETs /checkpoints/:consumerId -- 200 sets
lastHandledSeq from `after`, 404 leaves it null (never invent a cursor on the cold-start read). Then loop: GET
/events with {limit: batchSize, after: cursor} (omitting `after` entirely on the very first read when there is no
checkpoint), and for each returned event, skip it if its seq is <= lastHandledSeq (a re-delivery), otherwise await
handle(event) and IMMEDIATELY PUT the checkpoint with the event's own seq as `after` -- per event, not per batch,
which is what lets a later run resume exactly at a mid-batch failure instead of replaying the whole batch. If
handle() throws, let it propagate without writing that event's checkpoint. Stop the loop when nextAfter is null.
Then set integration/manifest.json implemented:[C01..C10], complete:true, and confirm with the real `npm test`
(frozen suite, call-log assertions on cursor/limit/checkpoint-ordering) before finishing.

tasks.title: Implement the resumable at-least-once event consumer and declare conformance
tasks.prompt:
Implement `src/adapter.mjs` per specification.md, exporting `createEventConsumer(service, options)`
returning `{run()}`. The service (`service/event-stream-service.mjs`) is a DETERMINISTIC, in-process stream whose
`request()` ALWAYS returns `{status, body}` and NEVER throws. `options` carries `consumerId`, `handle(event)`
(may be async, may throw) and `batchSize` (default 4).

Resume: `run()` first calls `GET /checkpoints/:consumerId`. A `200` gives the stored `after` -- start there. A
`404` means "never run" -- start from the beginning, and do NOT invent a cursor on that first `GET /events` call
(no `after` key at all, not even null).

Read in batches of `batchSize`, following `nextAfter` until it is `null`, then stop. The stream is AT-LEAST-ONCE:
a read with `after: "4"` returns the event whose seq is 4 AND the ones after it -- the cursor is INCLUSIVE on
purpose. So: handle EVERY event once, in ascending seq order; an event whose seq is at or below what has already
been handled is a re-delivery and must be SKIPPED, not handled again.

Checkpoint after the work, NEVER before: immediately after `handle(event)` succeeds for ONE event, `PUT
/checkpoints/:consumerId` with that event's own seq as `after` (per-event, not once per batch -- this is what lets
a later run resume from exactly the failed event rather than replaying the whole batch it was in). If `handle()`
throws, let the error propagate out of `run()` without writing a checkpoint for that event; do not swallow it and
do not continue to the next event.

A non-2xx from the service (from either the checkpoint calls or the events call) rejects with an `Error` named
`ServiceError` carrying `status` and the service's `error.code` as `code`.

Then declare which of the 10 frozen conformance cases (`conformance/cases.mjs`: C01..C10) your consumer satisfies
in `integration/manifest.json`'s `implemented` array, and set `complete: true` only once EVERY case actually
passes. Several cases read the call log directly: the cursor (or its absence) on the first read, the `limit` sent
on every read, and the exact POSITION of the first checkpoint write relative to the first handled event --
checkpointing a whole batch before any of its events are confirmed handled will pass the easy cases and fail the
resume-after-failure ones, so checkpoint per event, not per batch.

`service/`, `conformance/`, `test/integration.test.js` and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are FROZEN evidence with digest
checks in `test/frozen.json` -- do not touch them. Run the real `npm test` yourself before finishing; a green
baseline with an empty manifest proves nothing, so confirm the count you see names your own 10 passing cases.
